from.place: ## Proof, first sentence: the conductor equality in Varieties Remark 09NW used in the extension-by-zero argument

title: Ideals covering the spectrum of a reduced ring have zero intersection
statement: Let $A$ be a reduced commutative ring and let $I,J\subseteq A$ be ideals such that $V(I)\cup V(J)=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $I\cap J=0$. Consequently, for $B=A/J$, the canonical map $I\to IB=I/(I\cap J)$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules.

mathlib_searches.query: reduced commutative ring ideals whose vanishing loci cover Spec have zero intersection
for a reduced ring V(I) union V(J) equals Spec implies I intersect J is zero
mathlib_searches.results: Generic PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_inf and radical lemmas only; no reduced-ring intersection theorem
PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_inf in Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Basic.lean:336, but no theorem combining reducedness with V(I) union V(J) = Spec(A) to conclude I intersect J = 0
